destiny.title: One of the 54 paintings is yours
destiny.body: Every day of the year belongs to a card in the deck. Enter your birthday and we’ll show you which painting is yours.
destiny.joker_note: 31 December belongs to the Joker, who sits between the Ace of Hearts and the King of Spades. Pick whichever of the two paintings feels like yours.
destiny.missing_note: No card found for this date.

hero.lead_before: A deck of playing cards where
hero.lead_mark: every suit and rank hides inside a painting
hero.body: 54 works by Vasily Pochitsky across four worlds — from the gods of Olympus to the celebrities of our time. There are no pips or corner marks: you read each card from its scene, and the key comes in the box.
hero.deck_next: Show the next card in the deck

worlds_section.label: How to read the deck
worlds_section.title: Four worlds, four suits
worlds_section.lead: A classic 54-card deck — with scenes instead of pips. Ancient myth, the Middle Ages and modern culture, sorted into four suits.
worlds_section.mechanic: Suit and rank aren’t printed on the cards; they’re encoded in the details of each painting. Below is the key — the same one you’ll find in the booklet in the box.

worlds_check.label: Test yourself
worlds_check.question: Which world is this card from?
worlds_check.score_body: The suit is only the start — the full game asks you to read the rank as well.
worlds_check.image_alt: A card from the deck — guess its world

hearts.name: Olympic Gods
hearts.blurb: Desire, metamorphosis, prophecy and fire. Hearts are the ancient myths in which mortals argue with gods over their fate.

diamonds.name: Bearers of Secrets
diamonds.blurb: Alchemists, messengers and secret orders. Diamonds belong to those who hold knowledge that is never spoken aloud.

clubs.name: Templars
clubs.blurb: Crusader steel, treasure maps and the long shadow of the Order. Clubs carry medieval intrigue from vow to legend.

spades.name: Celebrities
spades.blurb: The myths of our own time. Faces everyone knows, turned into archetypes: Spades ask what happens when a public mask never comes off.

gallery.label: Gallery
gallery.title: See every card up close
gallery.hint: Tap a card to open it full size

authors.preface_p1: Long before Magister became a deck of cards, there were paintings.
authors.preface_p2: Vasily Pochitsky and Alexander Zhilchik spent years creating their own worlds — inventing characters, places and stories, and bringing them to life on canvas.
authors.preface_p3: Each of the 54 cards is based on one of these original works.
authors.preface_p4: The deck is only a glimpse into a much larger world.
authors.label: Authors
authors.title: Authors of Magister Cards

pochitsky.name: Vasily Pochitsky
pochitsky.role: Artist and co-creator of the Magister universe.
pochitsky.bio: Belarusian painter, illustrator and musician. He began painting in Rechitsa and went on to exhibit from Moscow to New York. For nearly a decade, his drawings appeared in the national press, and throughout his career he illustrated books and records.
pochitsky.bio_2: Magister was his most ambitious cycle: created in close collaboration with Alexander Zhilchik, the fifty-four paintings brought their shared world and its characters to life on canvas.

zhilchik.name: Alexander Zhilchik
zhilchik.bio: “I was lucky to be friends with a genius… and that was Vasya Pochitsky.”

authors.compact_body: Vasily Pochitsky (1967–2024) was a Belarusian painter, illustrator and musician from Rechitsa. His work was exhibited from Moscow to New York, ran in the national press for nearly a decade, and illustrated books and records. Magister is his largest cycle: 54 paintings of a world he invented with his friend Alexander Zhilchik. Vasily is gone. His world remains — in the paintings and in this deck.
authors.compact_quote: “I was lucky to be friends with a genius… and that was Vasya Pochitsky.”
authors.compact_quote_author: Alexander Zhilchik, creator of the concept

opportunity.label: Partnership
opportunity.title: Looking for the right partner
opportunity.lead: Magister is an original art-card IP. We keep authorship and seek partners for production and distribution.
opportunity.body_1: The art cycle is finished — fifty-four paintings, four worlds, a playable deck. We want a partner who can take the physical product further without taking the IP.
opportunity.body_2: SPIEL Essen 2026 is where we’d like to meet. Bring a conversation; we’ll bring the deck.

legacy.hero_lead_after: opening a gateway into an alternative mythology where alchemy, history and modernity intertwine.
legacy.hero_body: Each card is a fragment of this world — an artwork, a character and a story to explore, interpret and play with.

shop.title: Shop
